analysis: The PR changes only docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds one paragraph (head lines 532-546) documenting SSD eviction through SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest, using a linear SSDBlockIndex.oldest probe and then a bounded oldestFirstSnapshot heap. No source, configuration, protocol or deployment change is included, so no control is weakened here. The paragraph states that file leases, epoch validation and the store's removal lock still govern retirement. This matches the T-041 posture: per-file eviction is not an at-rest purge primitive, the KEK wipe remains the crypto purge, and the epoch is not rotated by eviction. It also matches the existing text at head lines 509-530, which says retirement validates the durable epoch/binding. The new text makes no claim of TTL or LRU purge on detached volumes, so it does not contradict the T-041 caveat about unmounted media. The 30-minute TTL, HMAC lookup tags and account-scoped cacheSalt are unchanged. The documentation says 'later changes cannot extend or reorder the pass'. The behavior cannot be checked here because SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.swift and SSDBlockIndex.swift are not in the supplied evidence. The next pass should confirm that the actual implementation, if changed in a companion PR, keeps the epoch and lease checks and does not delete entries owned by another epoch or binding. I examined the base excerpt (lines 853-953) and the head text (lines 1-857), and found no documentation drift that misstates a security control. The unchanged surrounding text is out of scope for this review.
